dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Sanitize/omit the raw decode-exception text in KIND_CONFIG_UNREADABLE so a malformed config's line fragment (which could contain a literal bearer value) is never echoed into doctor output.
evidence: _load_config returns `None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"` for `(UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError)` — the exception str for a JSON/TOML parse error commonly includes the offending source token/line fragment
_scan_client formats that into: `f"could not parse the {client} MCP config at {path}: {error}"` and returns it as the finding detail (KIND_CONFIG_UNREADABLE, lines ~186-193)
test_no_credential_value_reaches_findings_or_rendered_text only exercises well-formed configs, so this echo path is not covered by the leak-guard test

Module docstring asserts 'No credential VALUE ever enters a finding' — a malformed config containing an inline `Bearer <literal>` on a broken line is a reachability path that violates it since the parse never reaches the name-only extraction in _referenced_env_var
dropped.finding: The KIND_CONFIG_UNREADABLE finding embeds the raw JSON/TOML decode exception text into the finding detail; decode errors can quote a fragment of the offending config line, so a malformed config that contains a literal bearer PAT could have that credential fragment echoed into doctor's output (JSON + rendered text), contradicting the module's 'no credential value reaches a finding' invariant.
scenarios: Operator hand-edits ~/.claude.json, pastes a literal `Bearer <PAT>` value, and introduces a JSON syntax error on that line; running `rebar doctor` (esp. --output json) surfaces the JSONDecodeError message quoting the fragment, which is then pasted into a ticket/chat/CI log
dropped.suggested_fix: Report only the exception type and, at most, its line/column position (e.g. TOMLDecodeError/JSONDecodeError's `.lineno`/`.colno`) rather than `str(exc)`, so the offending source fragment is never included in the finding detail.
